rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to explore if combining RNA and image data improves performance. This tests the core hypothesis of multimodal profiling and isolates the effect of fusion (concat) and basic encoders (pca_n2000, resnet50). It balances exploration by starting with a simple multimodal setup while avoiding unnecessary complexity.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It is a logical extension of the previous configuration, balancing exploitation of the current model setting while exploring a key design choice (fusion method) that could significantly affect accuracy.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieves 0.526 validation accuracy. This experiment tests the effect of switching to multiprofile while keeping RNA/image encoders, aggregation, and fusion consistent. It isolates the impact of profile setting, a key design choice, and explores a promising direction without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_018) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6186). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (config_019) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It directly builds on the promising multiprofile direction while exploring a critical design choice with minimal changes.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with weighted fusion (config_019, 0.639) outperform others. This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (a key design choice) in the same setup, isolating its impact. Since transformer aggregation is untested in this context, it could reveal if this complex method improves accuracy further, balancing exploration of critical components while building on the current best configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve high accuracy (config_019: 0.639). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) while keeping other parameters the same (pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion). This isolates the effect of the image encoder, a critical design choice, and could reveal if upgrading the image encoder further improves performance. It balances exploitation of the successful multiprofile setup with exploration of a key component.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019, 025) achieve high validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while keeping other parameters the same, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploration of encoder alternatives with exploitation of the high-performing multiprofile/weighted fusion setup, targeting potential improvements in accuracy.

Existing evidence shows config_037 (avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests changing aggregation to transformer while keeping weighted fusion to isolate the effect of aggregation. It's the best use of the remaining budget as it explores a key design choice (aggregation method) that could significantly impact performance.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more advanced model) while keeping the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion settings can further improve performance. It directly compares RNA encoder choices under the same optimal configuration, clarifying whether scgpt outperforms scvi_n200 in this setup.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder and transformer aggregation but concat fusion, which could clarify if the fusion method (concat vs weighted) impacts performance. Since config_039 already uses weighted fusion, testing concat fusion with scgpt may reveal if this combination offers a trade-off or improvement, leveraging the remaining budget to explore critical design choices.
